reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes BitConnect lending in exchange for daily interest and an additional percentage while displaying high-return claims and an earnings calculator. He directs viewers to join through his referral URL and explains that signups through it earn him commissions, linking the investment promotion to his recruitment benefit. He acknowledges risk and advises viewers to invest only what they are willing to lose, while the records do not verify the advertised returns or referral payments.

you can use that money to lend the platform from a hundred to a hundred thousand dollars. And then you get, based on the Volatility Software Interest, which is this one. You can get some daily interest depending on that.
I've already done it actually, I have invested in BitConnect
if somebody else gets that link and signs up with it then you get a little commission from it
You can join bitconnect here for free: https://bitconnect.co/?ref=AndixIMA

opening.argument: Judge, this is a personal account of a speculative investment, not an assurance that viewers will profit. The speaker says BitConnect is risky and may remain profitable only while it lasts; he also tells viewers to limit any investment to what they can afford to lose. His discussion of interest is conditional, not a fixed promise. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether he is presenting investment commentary or deceptively certifying an opportunity.

citations.quote: Now I know a lot of people say that this is a really risky platform and it probably is, but as long as, as long as it is around
Only invest what you're willing to lose from the platform.
You can get some daily interest depending on that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited referral URL and commission explain a possible incentive, but neither proves that he promised a return or concealed the risk. The opening also calls the returns unverified; that is a reason to treat the figures cautiously, not proof that the speaker represented them as certain. He expressly calls the platform risky and limits what viewers should put in.

citations.quote: You can join bitconnect here for free: https://bitconnect.co/?ref=AndixIMA
Now I know a lot of people say that this is a really risky platform and it probably is
Only invest what you're willing to lose from the platform.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings do not change what he invites viewers to consider: putting money into BitConnect lending for daily interest. He describes his own investment and supplies a link for viewers to join. Acknowledging possible loss does not make an unverified return pitch mere market commentary, particularly when signups through the link can generate a commission for him.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation follows a newcomer explaining what he is doing across two platforms. He describes buying and selling Bitcoin on GDAX, explains how BitConnect lending works, and turns to the broader altcoin market as a subject for another video. Read as a first-person walkthrough, the lending figures are part of showing an interface and his experience, not proof that he guarantees anyone else's result. The video gives viewers a view of the process and its risks.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies a lending explanation, reported earnings, and a referral link. But explaining a feature and reporting one's own result do not, by themselves, establish a promise that viewers will earn the same amount. The speaker places the episode in a continuing discussion of Bitcoin and how he plans to invest, which supports reading it as a personal walkthrough.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still promote an investment. The speaker explains how viewers can lend money for daily interest, reports substantial lending profit, and provides a link to join. His stated plan to keep covering Bitcoin does not erase the concrete BitConnect lending pitch or the referral incentive tied to signups.

opening.argument: Judge, the evidence shows a discussion of a financial service and an openly disclosed referral arrangement, not a demonstrated deception by this speaker. He says a signup through a link can earn him a commission and reports that he has no referred people so far. The description invites viewers to join for free. None of that establishes a guaranteed return, a request for credentials, or that any viewer paid him. The cited material shows an incentive to promote the service; it does not establish those further steps.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest point is the combination of a lending pitch and referral benefit. But its own citations describe interest as dependent on a variable and commission as contingent on someone signing up. They do not show a guaranteed payout or an actual referral payment. The existence of a disclosed incentive should be weighed, not treated as proof of a hidden transaction.

Calling entry free does not address the capital he says users can lend afterward.
